mistakes.why: That adds the two triangles' areas, 2 + 4.5. The triangle from 3 to 6 lies below the axis and subtracts.
The sign is reversed: the larger triangle, area 4.5, is below the axis, so the result is negative.

items.q: For the function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> in a free-response question, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = \int_0^x f(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is graphed. Which sentence earns the point for "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has a relative maximum at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>"?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(5) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(5) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down.

The graph changes from going up to going down at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(x) = f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> changes from positive to negative at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = \int_0^x \cos(t^2)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 2</annotation></semantics></math>. At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> have a relative maximum?

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(t^2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^2 = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so take the square root: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \sqrt{\pi/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>π</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \sqrt{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(t^2) = \cos \pi = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0. The first zero is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^2 = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = \int_0^x \left(e^{\sin t} - 1.5\right)dt</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Use a calculator to find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> at which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has a relative maximum.

mistakes.why: At this zero of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\sin x} - 1.5</annotation></semantics></math> changes from negative to positive: that is a relative minimum. The maximum is at the other zero in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3, 7]</annotation></semantics></math> together make <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 7]</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 f + \int_3^7 f = \int_0^7 f</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtract 5 from 12; do not add.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 f(x)\,dx = 12 - 5</annotation></semantics></math>, positive. The minus sign would come from writing the limits the other way, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_7^3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_7^3 \left(2f(x) - g(x)\right)dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7</annotation></semantics></math>. The limits here run from 7 down to 3, which flips the sign.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 g(x)\,dx = -2</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtracting it adds 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(7) - (-2) = 16</annotation></semantics></math>, then flip the sign.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 \left(f(x) + 4\right)dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The constant 4 is integrated over an interval 4 wide: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mn>4</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 4\,dx = 4 \cdot 4 = 16</annotation></semantics></math>, not 4.

That is only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mn>4</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 4\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 f(x)\,dx = 7</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^7 g(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_3^7 g(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>; adding it lowers the total: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + (-2) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Additivity adds the two pieces: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + (-2)</annotation></semantics></math>, not their product.

items.q: Split <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-4, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> where the pieces of the graph change and add the signed areas. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-4}^{4} f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The semicircle lies below the axis, so its area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is subtracted.

The region on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-4, 0]</annotation></semantics></math> is half a disc: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 = 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

On <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> the height is 1, not 2: that rectangle has area 2. The jump at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> matters.

items.q: Watch the order of the limits: find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>4</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_4^0 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. With the limits reversed the value changes sign.

On <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so that rectangle has area 2. The triangle on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2]</annotation></semantics></math> also has area 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 f = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> the graph passes from the semicircle to the segment. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> to 0 the graph is a quarter circle below the axis: subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> to 0 is only half of the semicircle: a quarter disc, area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}\pi(2)^2 = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> has a jump at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Can <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> still be found, and if so, what is it?
options: Yes, it is 2, counting the area on [0, 2] and leaving out the rest
Yes, it is 4; a single jump does not stop it

Decreasing: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.606</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D'(6) \approx -1.606</annotation></semantics></math>

Increasing, because the depth <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(6)</annotation></semantics></math> is greater than <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(0)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At what time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 8]</annotation></semantics></math> is the snow deepest?

mistakes.why: At this zero of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D'</annotation></semantics></math>, the rate changes from negative to positive: the depth is at a low point there, not a high one.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D' < 0</annotation></semantics></math> from about 5.422 to 8, so the snow is melting at the end: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>9.413</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(8) \approx 9.413</annotation></semantics></math> is less than the depth at 5.422.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^3 (3x^2 - 2)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(1) = 1^3 - 2(1) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(3) - F(1) = 21 - (-1) = 22</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtracting a negative adds.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(3)</annotation></semantics></math> alone. Subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(1) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: An antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> (its derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math>), not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{2} - \sin 0 = 1 - 0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. A value of 0 would come from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the integrand, not an antiderivative.

items.q: Use the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> to evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^{e} \frac{1}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> as the antiderivative. An antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> in the wrong direction. The function whose derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 e^x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(1)</annotation></semantics></math> alone. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(0) = e^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0, so subtract 1.

items.q: A town's population is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(t)</annotation></semantics></math> thousand people, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> years after 1990. What does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>30</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{30} P'(t)\,dt = 12</annotation></semantics></math> mean?
options: The population grew by 12 thousand people from 1990 to 2020
The population was 12 thousand people in the year 2020
The population grew at a rate of 12 thousand people per year
The population grew by 12 thousand people in each of the years

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1) = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^6 h'(x)\,dx = -3</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(6)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Read the derivative of the inverse tangent backward to evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{1}{1 + x^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(1 + x^2)</annotation></semantics></math> has derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2x}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The function whose derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan 1 = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(x) = \int_1^x (2t + 1)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>. Write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(x)</annotation></semantics></math> without an integral sign.

mistakes.why: Subtract the antiderivative at the lower limit too: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^2 + x) - (1^2 + 1) = x^2 + x - 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(1)</annotation></semantics></math> must be 0.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. The question asks for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(x)</annotation></semantics></math> itself, an antiderivative evaluated from 1 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int (3x^2 - 4x + 1)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include the constant: write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That differentiates. An antiderivative goes the other way: raise each power by one and divide by the new power.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 4x\,dx = 4 \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} = 2x^2</annotation></semantics></math>: divide by the new power, 2.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 3x^2\,dx = 3 \cdot \frac{x^3}{3} = x^3</annotation></semantics></math>; the coefficient 3 cancels with the new power.

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x + C</annotation></semantics></math>. Find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> that makes the graph pass through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: 5 is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2)</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>. Substitute: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 8 - 8 + 2 + C = 2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, and set it equal to 5.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + C = 5</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtract 2 from 5; do not add.

items.q: Write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The constant is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 2 + C = 5</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 0</annotation></semantics></math> the graph passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 5)</annotation></semantics></math> to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Using the function you found, evaluate it at the origin: what is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = 6x</annotation></semantics></math> with no constant. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(0) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> means <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = 6x + 2</annotation></semantics></math>, which adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 3x^2 + 2x + C</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> means <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; it was left out.

items.q: With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 1 + x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, what does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> become?
What are the limits of integration in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which integral in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 x(1 + x^2)^3\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 x(1 + x^2)^3\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That keeps the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-limits 0 and 1 with the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>-integral: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{u^4}{4}\Big|_0^1</annotation></semantics></math>. Change the limits to 1 and 2.

The factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}du</annotation></semantics></math> was dropped.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int u^3\,du = \frac{u^4}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>: divide by 4 as well as by 2.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^3 f'(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) - f(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. An antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(g(x))g'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>, so evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(3) = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The order is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(3)) - f(g(1)) = f(4) - f(2) = 1 - 3</annotation></semantics></math>: subtract, do not add.

items.q: The substitution <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> turns <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^3 f'(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> into which integral?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^3 f'(u)\,du</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^4 f'(u)\,g'(u)\,du</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-1}^{-3} f'(u)\,du</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^4 f'(u)\,du</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^2 g'(x)\,e^{g(x)}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That evaluates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> at 2 and 1. The antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{g(x)}</annotation></semantics></math>, so use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2) = 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Upper limit first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{g(2)} - e^{g(1)} = e^5 - e^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^3 \frac{g'(x)}{g(x)}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is positive on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>.)

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 3 - \ln 1</annotation></semantics></math>, using the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-limits. The antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|g(x)|</annotation></semantics></math>: evaluate at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(3) = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That evaluates the integrand <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{g'(x)}{g(x)}</annotation></semantics></math> at 3 and 1 and subtracts. Evaluate an antiderivative instead: with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> it is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|u|</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 2x\cos(x^2)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The factors cannot be integrated separately. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> and the integral is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \cos u\,du = \sin u</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \cos u\,du = \sin u</annotation></semantics></math>, with a plus sign.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int e^{3x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{3x}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3e^{3x}</annotation></semantics></math>. To undo that factor 3, divide by 3.

That is the derivative. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 3x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = \frac{1}{3}du</annotation></semantics></math>: divide by 3.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \cos(5x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(5x)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\cos(5x)</annotation></semantics></math>, so you need <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> in front, not 5.

Its derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\cos(5x)</annotation></semantics></math>, five times too big. Divide by 5.

items.q: Substitute for the denominator and antidifferentiate: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x}{x^2 + 4}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}du</annotation></semantics></math>: the answer has a factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The arctan form is for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 4}</annotation></semantics></math> with no <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> on top. Here the top is (half) the derivative of the bottom: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2 + 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{\ln x}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math> the integral is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int u\,du = \frac{u^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: keep the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That would come from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x\ln x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> is on top: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = \frac{1}{x}dx</annotation></semantics></math>, and the integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\,du</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \sin^3 x \cos x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int u^3\,du = \frac{u^4}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>: divide by the new power.

The inside function is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>, whose derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is the other factor. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>, and the answer is in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><msqrt><mi>π</mi></msqrt></msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\sqrt{\pi}} x\sin(x^2)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That evaluates the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>-antiderivative at the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-limits. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2</annotation></semantics></math> the limits become 0 and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}du</annotation></semantics></math>: the answer is half of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^\pi \sin u\,du = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>u</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 x e^{x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^2 e^u\,du</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>. What is wrong?
options: Nothing is wrong; the limits stay the same for any substitution
The limits were not changed: they should be u = 0 to u = 4

The substitution should be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = e^{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>
